10A.
Public Hearing to consider two appeals of the Planning and Building Director's legal nonconforming use determination involving agricultural operations and accessory uses taking place at 598 Park Lane, commonly referred to as "Coral Tree Farm." PROPERTY OWNER: Laurel Mehl; APPELLANTS: Jodie Paxton (neighbor) and Catherine Blakespear (representing the property owner); LOCATION: 598 Park Lane (APN: 258-252-59). Contact Person: Senior Planner Kusiak
Uphold the determination of the Planning and Building Director for the reasons discussed in the "Analysis" section of this Agenda Report (specifically Sections B & D). Should the Council elect this option, staff recommends that the Council determine whether the operations should be allowed to continue while a minor use permit is pursued and identify a reasonable time period to secure said permit. Possible alternative actions can be found in Section E of the Analysis section.
PLEASE NOTE THAT DUE TO THE LARGE SIZE OF THIS DOCUMENT, IT MAY TAKE A FEW MINUTES TO LOAD.
2014-09-24 Item 10A - Coral Tree Farm Appeal
10B.
Public Hearing regarding the introduction of City Council Ordinance 2014-09, Option A or B, to consider a Zoning Code Amendment to Title 30 of the Encinitas Municipal Code and the Home Depot Specific Plan, pursuant to Council direction related to Item 10E of the July 16, 2014 City Council meeting, to amend the definition of 'Net Acreage' to specify that detention basins and wetlands (rather than significant wetlands) are excluded from net acreage. Sections being considered for amendment include Section 30.16.010(B)(2) and 30.04 (Chapter Definitions) of the Encinitas Municipal Code and Section III.F.1.a of the Home Depot Specific Plan. CASE NUMBER: 14-177 ZCA/LCPA; APPLICANT: City of Encinitas; LOCATION: City-wide. Contact Person: Principal Planner Langager
At their meeting of September 4, 2014, the Planning Commission considered the proposed code amendments, both Options A and B, and made recommendation to the City Council to adopt draft Ordinance 2014-09, Option B with the addition of "detention basins" in the proposed definition of "regulatory required stormwater facilities". Resolution PC-2014-23 includes the Planning Commission's formal recommendation. As part of their discussion, the Planning Commission noted that density needs to be addressed in further detail as part of the Housing Element Update; the revisions to net acreage are a short-term solution until the update can be completed. The Commission further noted that Option B is a way in which to define/clarify detention basins in order to implement Council's original direction more effectively and clearly. The Planning Commission was also concerned with exactly what the various stormwater treatment facilities are, as identified in the definition for "regulatory required stormwater facilities". Staff noted that these facilities are depicted in the City's Stormwater Manual.The Planning Commission was also concerned about unintended consequences associated with the proposed amendments, which was one of the reasons for the dissenting vote.
2014-09-24 Item 10B - Net Acreage Public Hearing

ADJOURNMENT
Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
